issue.title: Task-bead backlog, epic 2: fix the five most important open task beads
issue.description: The five most important workable task beads in the sase project are resolved on master and closed with recorded evidence: sase-1og (the check-full flake-baseline gate exits 2 before judging anything), sase-18t (ToolRun store "database is locked" under parallel load), sase-1a7 (the Files ctrl+j anchor-scroll node that keeps Full CI red), sase-12f (the monitor-capacity fakey e2e that exits 124 under load), and sase-1ot (owner-approved rotation and purge of 27 historical secret-scanner hits in public sase--agents history). The land agent then starts the next backlog epic, five beads at a time, until no workable task bead remains.

issue.title: Make the flake-baseline gate reach a truthful verdict again (sase-1og)

issue.title: Stop the ToolRun store failing with "database is locked" under parallel load (sase-18t)

payload.entry: PLANNING EVIDENCE: At clean base e608de2db6 the unchanged target passed once in 65.58s, with 61.89s test-call time and 60.608s in settle_named_proc before successor startup. The shared fakey harness creates flat ace-run timestamp paths, while production starter settlement uses canonical date-sharded paths. An in-memory diagnostic probe using canonical agent paths preserved all assertions and five-second budgets and passed in 4.32s total / 1.85s call; the real starter-settlement wait saw done.json already present and returned True immediately. No source implementation edits were made. This proves the wasted settlement wait, not the historical load-only exit-124 cause. The validated medium tale sase_plan_capacity_e2e_load_robust.md requires comparable isolated and loaded before/after evidence before closure. epic-symbols reported no entries for this phase.

Phase sase-1ou.4 evidence (before monitor handoff):

Cause: Files spread Ctrl-J race had two backlog-era gaps. (1) Hidden paged AgentFilePanel shares the same VerticalScroll as FilesSpreadView; its anchor capture/restore had no visibility guard, so a delayed static-read restore reset spread scroll_y 6->0 (reproduced deterministically). (2) Spread navigation used an 8-attempt call_after_refresh chain with no pending state; late anchors/reserve after the burst abandoned the request. Rapid Ctrl-J also recomputed from stale scroll_y instead of pending, and the scroll watcher re-derived during flight.

Fix (presentation-only, this repo):
- src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/file_panel/_content.py: hidden paged view never captures or applies scroll anchors (_is_hidden_for_scroll guard in _capture/_apply/_note_slot_change).
- src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/decks/panel_spread.py: pending Files navigation (_files_pending_scroll_index/generation/retry/confirmed), immediate scroll_to, two-consecutive confirm, layout resume via _reschedule_files_scroll_after_layout, superseding chains from pending, unmount clears.
- src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/decks/files_spread.py: _publish_section_layout resumes pending navigation.
- src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/decks/panel_files.py: transitions and new-subject probe bump generation and clear pending.
- src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/decks/panel.py: leaving spread clears pending.
- src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/decks/panel_interaction.py: scroll watcher holds pending page instead of re-deriving.
- tests/ace/tui/widgets/decks/test_files_anchor_ownership.py: 4 real-widget regression tests (hidden restore, visible restore+return offset, supersede+manual hold, late-layout resume).
